mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility is the highest-frequency proxy for discretionary trip-making; the t-0w improvement of TRANSIT from -72.7 to -64.7 marks a turning point in trip capacity that feeds retail-and-recreation footfall with a multi-week lag, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -72.7 at t-1w to -64.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the 28 days after 2021-06-15 is at or below its mean over the prior 28 days even though TRANSIT continues to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week jump in RETAIL_REC of more than 15 points marks the release of pent-up discretionary demand after a mobility trough; once crossed, that release propagates for roughly two weeks, lifting the four-week mean of RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change exceeds +15 points (t-1w -43.4 to t-0w -24.4)
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC jumped +19.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: Within 14 days of the threshold crossing, RETAIL_REC falls back below its t-1w level of -43.4 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery needs both trip capacity and a destination reason: only when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve jointly in the same week does commuting-linked after-work and lunchtime footfall rebuild, producing higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve in the same weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT -72.7 to -64.7 and WORKPLACES -33.7 to -30.7 both improved at t-0w
failure_condition: Following weeks in which TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is no higher than following weeks in which only one of them improves.

mechanism_narrative: Under an active reopening regime, outdoor congregation is normalized before indoor capacity limits are lifted, so the PARKS rebound from -43.0 at t-2w to -34.0 at t-0w leads indoor retail-and-recreation recovery by about two weeks.
candidate_trigger: Regime classified as reopening with PARKS improving in two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -43.0 at t-2w to -34.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening with phased lifting of restrictions
failure_condition: In the two weeks after a PARKS improvement under the reopening regime, RETAIL_REC is flat or lower relative to its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains +14.4 percent above baseline at t-0w even as every activity series partially recovers, showing that home-confinement habits have not unwound; residual stay-at-home behavior caps weekday retail footfall, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays above +10 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was +18.9 at t-1w and +14.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the 7 days after 2021-06-15 is higher than its prior 7-day value while RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 percent.

mechanism_narrative: Onset of the Madrid summer pushes leisure spending outdoors; PARKS rising from -43.0 at t-2w to -34.0 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated signals substitution away from enclosed retail-and-recreation venues, lowering indoor RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 percent
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS +6.4 points and RESIDENTIAL -4.5 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its prior 28-day mean while PARKS keeps rising and RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 percent.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w retail rebound of +19.0 points far outpaces the transit improvement of only +8.0 points, opening a wide TRANSIT-to-RETAIL_REC divergence; retail footfall cannot be sustained without matching trip volume, so the gap closes by RETAIL_REC falling back within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -60 while RETAIL_REC is above -30 in the same weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the 7 days after 2021-06-15 is above -24.4 percent while TRANSIT remains below -60 percent.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES improving from -33.7 to -30.7 reflects the unwinding of telework mandates; restored office occupancy rebuilds weekday lunchtime and after-work retail demand within two weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean improves by more than 2 points week-on-week (t-1w -33.7 to t-0w -30.7)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved +3.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the 14 days after 2021-06-15 stays at or below its prior 14-day mean while WORKPLACES keeps improving.
